title: Autoscaler backpressure oscillation causing microburst starvation for small tenants — patch + customer comms
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several small-tenant customers (multi-tenant Dedicated pools and a private deployment) experienced repeated ~30–90s tail-latency spikes and request drops during microburst traffic patterns between 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-12. Root cause analysis indicates the autoscaler’s backpressure logic oscillated under high-cardinality burst conditions: short-lived queue growth triggered conservative scale-down windows while concurrent KV-cache eviction + slot preemption policy removed warm slots, producing a feedback loop that prevented timely refill of headroom for small tenants.

Impact: Intermittent customer request failures, increased cold starts, and transient SLA violations for 7 customers (severity escalations from two mid-market customers). Affected tenants were small (low steady QPS) but bursty (short traffic spikes). Private tenant ACME-42 reported degraded end-user experience and opened an escalation.

Repro steps: 1) Simulate 10s microbursts at 5–10x baseline QPS across many small-tenants; 2) Observe autoscaler: scale-down heuristics fire during quiet windows; 3) KV cache eviction policy aggressively frees memory when headroom dips; 4) Combined effect produces slot shortage when next burst arrives.

Root cause (technical): The autoscaler backpressure estimator uses a smoothed headroom metric (ema over 60s) that undervalues short-term burst risk for small tenants. When many small tenants emit staggered bursts, the estimator alternates between scale-up signals and immediate conservative scale-down signals due to a short safety window. Additionally, the slot-preemption path currently marks slots as reclaimable without coordinating with the prefix/KV cache hotness signals. This causes warm slot churn and increases cold-start cost.

Immediate mitigations already applied (hotfix + ops):
- Increased autoscaler safety window for all Dedicated pools in region eu-west-1 to 120s (temporary config) to prevent premature scale-downs.
- Disabled aggressive slot-preemption for tenants with average < 50 QPS across last 30m.
- Rolled priority fallback to compatible model variants for impacted customers to reduce load during bursts.
- Customer comms: Sent interim message to ACME-42 and two other customers (see comments).

Planned permanent fix (owner: Liam O'Connor):
1) Replace 60s EMA with a two-timescale estimator (fast-reacting short-window + conservative long-window) that factors tenant burstiness score. (design-doc: Confluence link below)
2) Gate slot-preemption with KV-cache-hotness signal: do not reclaim slots with recent prefix hits above threshold.
3) Add small-tenant-aware headroom floor: keep minimal reserved slots for tenants with burst patterns.
4) Add unit+load tests that simulate high-cardinality microbursts and validate no oscillation.

Rollout plan: Canary in eu-west-1 (low-risk tenants) for 48h -> monitor burst loss, tail-latency and reserved-slot churn -> extend to global Dedicated pools. Feature flag gated; rollback path prepared. Target release: runtime-1.36 patch (hotfix branch) with follow-up runtime-1.37 improvement.

Monitoring and acceptance criteria:
- 95th and 99th tail latency during burst windows reduced by >= 30% vs baseline within canary tenants.
- No customer-facing 5xx incidents for same traffic replay.
- New telemetry shows persistent headroom floor for small tenants.

Communication: Draft customer-facing postmortem and runbook update ready for review. Notify Support and CSM teams prior to canary release.
